title: SiO2/Al2O3 multi-cavity stack for sharp bandpass edges
scientific_hypothesis: A multi-cavity design using SiO2 and Al2O3 with three defect layers will produce sharper bandpass edges than a single-cavity design, enabling better separation between the 255-280 nm passband and the 300+ nm stopbands.
design_principle: Multiple coupled cavities create a flatter passband top and steeper edges through mode coupling. SiO2 and Al2O3 both have excellent UV transparency, minimizing passband absorption. The trade-off is increased layer count and optimization complexity.
proposed_topology: air | (sio2 | al2o3)_6 | sio2 | (al2o3 | sio2)_4 | al2o3 | (sio2 | al2o3)_4 | sio2 | (al2o3 | sio2)_6 | sio2_substrate
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 25 film layers
manufacturing_considerations: 25 layers within 30-layer limit but leaves little margin
SiO2 and Al2O3 are highly conventional deposition materials
Three cavities require precise thickness matching for mode coupling
theory_basis: Multi-cavity filter design for flat-top bandpass
Transfer matrix method for complex multilayer stacks
expected_advantages: Sharper bandpass edges improve stopband rejection near passband
SiO2 and Al2O3 have minimal UV absorption
Flat-top passband better covers the full 255-280 nm range
known_risks: Three cavities increase optimization complexity and risk of local minima
May be more sensitive to thickness errors than single-cavity design
execution_request_english: Design a multi-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate. Stack topology: air incident medium, then 6 repeated pairs of SiO2 (Gao) and al2o3 (SiO2 (Gao) first), followed by a SiO2 (Gao) defect cavity, then 4 repeated pairs of al2o3 and SiO2 (Gao) (al2o3 first), followed by an al2o3 defect cavity, then 4 repeated pairs of SiO2 (Gao) and al2o3 (SiO2 (Gao) first), followed by a SiO2 (Gao) defect cavity, then 6 repeated pairs of al2o3 and SiO2 (Gao) (al2o3 first), terminating on SiO2 (Gao) substrate. Total film layers: 25. All 25 layer thicknesses are optimizable design variables. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Total layers must not exceed 30.
